text:
Maria Gutierrez: Quick heads-up — proposing a tiny refactor to unify the per-model adapter layer. Goal: reduce compatibility debt between smokehouse and runtime probes.
Ashok Patel: TL;DR — what's the main pain? more brittle adapters or duplicated golden sampling logic?
Maria Gutierrez: Both. Right now we have 3 adapter variants: 'intake', 'bench', 'runtime'. Lots of subtle divergences cause flakes in accept/reject decisions.
Lin Huang: Can you sketch the proposed shape?
Maria Gutierrez: Sure. Idea: single Adapter API surface that expresses 3 orthogonal hooks: transform_descriptor, sample_for_smoke, runtime_handshake. Implementations can be thin wrappers.
Taylor Reed: I like orthogonality. Concern: we already gate tests on the bench sampling outputs. Do we risk regression during migration?
Maria Gutierrez: Migration plan: feature-flag adapters + auto-compat layer that forwards to legacy adapters when feature flag off. Gradual rollout per model family.
Jen Cho: What about perf? unified adapter might add a hop on hot path.
Lin Huang: We can keep hot path inlined. The unified API is for control plane and bench; runtime-critical code can depend on a small fastpath interface.
Ashok Patel: How will acceptance criteria look? We need clear numbers so QA can sign off.
Maria Gutierrez: Proposal draft in bullet form:
- No change in bench golden outputs for 95% of models during migration window
- Latency overhead < 1ms p95 on runtime serve path
- One-week shadowing with canary models
- Rollback signal if smoke pass rate drops by > 3% absolute
Taylor Reed: Where do we measure those? bench-bot telemetry? console metrics?
Maria Gutierrez: bench-bot will emit sample diffs and a 'golden-stability' score. Console will show per-model delta, with alerting thresholds.
bench-bot: new report available: https://internal/reports/adapter-proposal/1744300000
Ashok Patel: Nice. About compatibility checks — are we adding new linting on descriptor changes?
Maria Gutierrez: Yes. Linter rules:
- disallow removing tokenizer/shape fields without 'compat: major' flag
- warn when changing kv-cache semantics
- require a smoke input set for any quantized binary changes
Lin Huang: For quantized binaries, we should require a small 'golden' embedding check to detect rounding drift.
Jen Cho: Also add an invariant check that runtime_handshake doesn't change required env vars
Taylor Reed: Can we keep the old adapters as a shim long-term? That creates debt.
Maria Gutierrez: Plan to deprecate shims after 3 months of zero regressions per model family.
Ashok Patel: What about model families that are low-traffic? They might not reach the canary window worthily.
Maria Gutierrez: For low-traffic models, run a synthetic traffic harness nightly for 2 weeks and base decision on that.
Lin Huang: Who owns the migration runbook? Eng-ML or Eng-Platform?
Maria Gutierrez: Joint ownership. Eng-ML owns adapters, Eng-Platform owns rollout and metrics plumbing.
Taylor Reed: OK. I'm +1 for the API shape. Can we get a PR with interfaces and the sample diff tooling?
Maria Gutierrez: Will send PR by EOD. Link to short RFC draft: https://internal/rfcs/adapter-unify/1744300000
Jen Cho: Add a checklist item for security review (env var changes, KMS access for private deployments).
Maria Gutierrez: Good call, added.
Taylor Reed: One last ask — include a migration dashboard widget summarizing per-model 'compat health' (green/yellow/red) so we can triage.
bench-bot: created dashboard ticket #ENGML-4872
Maria Gutierrez: Thanks all. I'll post the PR and tag reviewers. If no objections by EOD tomorrow, we'll cut a canary branch.
Ashok Patel: Sounds good.
Lin Huang: Thanks!
Taylor Reed: :thumbsup:
Jen Cho: :+1:
